spec.name: Saadian Tombs
spec.description: The Saadian Tombs are a royal necropolis in the Kasbah of Marrakech and one of the city's most important monuments from the Saadian period. The site contains the graves of members of the Saadian dynasty, including Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur and members of his family. Although burials existed here before his reign, Ahmad al-Mansur transformed the necropolis in the late 16th century with richly decorated mausoleums. The complex is renowned for its carved cedar wood, stucco, marble columns, geometric tilework and the celebrated Chamber of the Twelve Columns. After the fall of the Saadian dynasty, the tombs became largely enclosed and were eventually brought to wider modern attention in the early 20th century.

access.comment: Admission fees and opening conditions may change. Moroccan nationals can benefit from free admission on Fridays and on the first day of national and religious holidays under the Ministry of Culture's monument admission policy.

timeline.title: Burial of Muhammad al-Shaykh
timeline.description: The Saadian ruler Muhammad al-Shaykh was buried at the site, establishing an important royal burial presence in the Kasbah.

timeline.title: Reign of Ahmad al-Mansur
timeline.description: Ahmad al-Mansur became sultan and subsequently developed the necropolis into an elaborate royal funerary complex.

timeline.title: Burial of Ahmad al-Mansur
timeline.description: Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur was buried in the monumental mausoleum he had developed for the Saadian royal family.

timeline.title: Modern rediscovery
timeline.description: The Saadian Tombs were brought to wider modern attention during the French Protectorate period and subsequently studied and restored.
